title: Singleton masses of a good conditional special-pair law
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the disjointness problem on inputs of length $n$, drawn under the hard distribution. Write $(x_T, y_T)$ for the pair of Alice's and Bob's bits at the special coordinate $T$, and for a value $z$ of the conditioning statistic let $\mu_z$ denote the conditional law of this bit-pair on $\{0,1\}^2$ given that the statistic equals $z$. Suppose $z$ is $\gamma$-good, in the sense that the total variation distance between $\mu_z$ and the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^2$ is at most $2\gamma$. Then for every bit-pair $b \in \{0,1\}^2$,
\[
  \abs{\mu_z(\{b\}) - \tfrac{1}{4}} \le 2\gamma .
\]
hypotheses_covered: p a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length n
z a value of the conditioning statistic
z is gamma-good: total variation distance of its conditional special-pair law from the uniform law on bit-pairs is at most 2*gamma
replaced: A good $z$ gives the expected singleton-mass estimate for the conditional special-pair law.
